topic: Legal ops ROI: Cooley’s GO Public
angle: AI that upgrades judgment by clearing the runway of legal busywork is where enterprise value shows up.
sourceTitle: How Cooley is accelerating IPO work with ChatGPT
linkedinPost:
AI that ships work product beats AI that ships demos.

OpenAI profiled Cooley’s “GO Public,” which uses AI to surface issues earlier in IPO workflows so lawyers can spend time on judgment, not document spelunking.

This is the pattern I see in enterprise wins: don’t automate the lawyer—automate the legal rummaging. When the system pre-reads filings, flags inconsistencies, and assembles a first draft checklist, senior reviewers concentrate on risk calls and negotiation strategy. Throughput goes up. Error rates go down. Morale improves because people do actual lawyering.

If you’re replicating this playbook in your org:
- Define a measurable “review ready” state. Time-to-ready is the KPI.
- Treat AI as a routing and prep layer that upgrades human judgment.
- Build audit trails and redlines into the flow; compliance loves receipts.

I’d rather see a 30% faster “issue surfacing” stage than a flashy chatbot no one trusts. That’s where compounding ROI starts.

What’s the heaviest prep step in your process—and how would better “review ready” change outcomes? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AITransformation
